findings (all optional, none a regression from `b46fa93`; each fails to the permission prompt or was already allowed on the base):
1. `workflow-check.ts:~2185` (`comesFromArgs`): any reference to a function binding counts as data from `args`. So `let s='aa'; const f=()=>s; for(...40){ s=s.replaceAll('a', f()) }` is allowed (confirmed). It needs a deliberately crafted script. Smallest fix: treat a function binding as not from `args` unless its return value comes from `args`.
2. `workflow-check.ts:~1953` (`separatorsOf`): `[...lines].join('\n')` is treated as a character split. Round-tripping `out.split('\n')` through a spread therefore refuses with "uses one value twice" (confirmed). It is a false refusal that falls back to the prompt. Smallest fix: judge `[...x]` and `Array.from(x)` as `""` only when `x` is not itself an array derived from a split.
3. `workflow-check.ts:~1959`: `s.split('').map(c=>c).join('--')` and `const [a,...rest]=s; rest.join('--')` in a loop are allowed (confirmed). Both were allowed on the base. Smallest fix: refuse a join whose receiver derives from a string split or spread but passes through another method.
4. `scripts/vendor.ts:~105`: a failed download is reported twice (the `failed` message, then the `X is missing` problems). Cosmetic.
